scenarios.name: Report hides Keleo internals from reader
given: a report is generated from a practice or method
then: no Keleo-specific terms appear (alpha, state, activitySpace, workProduct, narrativeType, baseline, contributesTo, mapsTo, relatesTo, checklist item, level of detail, practice language)
the report reads as a standalone document requiring no Keleo knowledge

scenarios.name: Narrative structure drives report organization
given: a narrative type is selected from the baseline
then: each top-level section maps to a narrative element from the selected type
section headings are plain English (not raw narrative element names unless naturally appropriate)

scenarios.name: Practice knowledge informs report content
given: a practice or method provides domain knowledge
then: the analytical framework from the practice shapes the report's dimensions, criteria, and recommendations
practice concepts are translated into plain language appropriate to the audience

scenarios.name: Report attribution is minimal and optional
given: a report is generated
then: at most one brief line at the end attributes the analytical framework
no structural diagrams, schema references, or methodology deep-dives are included

scenarios.name: Framework attribution links to keleo-studio-gas
given: a report closes with a framework attribution line
keleo-studio-gas is configured in `.claude/user-config.json`
then: every practice, method, or baseline named in it is a markdown hyperlink
each link is a `?doc=<document name>` deep link on the configured deployment
the line is generated with `studio-client.py --link ... --attribution`, not hand-written

scenarios.name: Report is a self-contained directory
given: a reporting skill generates a report
then: the report lives at `reports/<report-slug>/<report-slug>.md`
its diagram specs and rendered SVGs live in `reports/<report-slug>/assets/`
every embedded diagram path is relative to the markdown and resolves

scenarios.name: Session provenance is recorded and closed
given: a reporting skill completes a run
then: `00-prompt-history.md` is present alongside the report
it records the user's prompt, each practice/method resolved as a dependency, and the narrative strategy decision
it lists the report as a deliverable
the session is finalized

scenarios.name: Report is linted and verified before handover
given: a report has been written to its workspace
when: the report is handed to the user, exported, or published
then: `lint-report.py` has been run with all checks and reports no errors
the verification gate has been run with `--expect` naming every verifier launched
no blocking error survives reconciliation
the verdict is recorded in `00-prompt-history.md` as a decision
both ran before any PDF export or Google Doc publish

scenarios.name: Diagnosis explains the mechanism
given: a report evaluates a strategy against operating conditions
then: it connects evidence to the mechanism affecting the outcome and the affected participants
it distinguishes sourced facts from inferred consequences

scenarios.name: Commercial recommendations test mutual value
given: a report recommends an offer or investment
then: it identifies the buyer, outcome, participant benefits and costs, and contracting, billing, delivery and support responsibilities
missing evidence is explicit rather than replaced by invented economics

scenarios.name: Actions address constraints in dependency order
given: implementation recommendations are within the agreed scope
then: priority actions trace to findings and specify a role, prerequisite and success evidence
blockers precede dependent activities and proposed commitments are labelled

scenarios.name: Analysis respects the requested scope
given: an informational or comparison-only report is requested
then: causal analysis remains within that scope without an unsolicited execution plan
prose explains the argument while tables support comparison or execution detail

scenarios.name: Claims are grounded or owned
given: a report makes a factual claim, statistic, benchmark, or attributed recommendation
then: the claim traces to the effective context, traces to a cited source, or is the report's own analysis
a quantified claim with no source is reported as an error
the report's own analysis reads as analysis rather than as established fact

scenarios.name: Cited works exist and support their claims
given: a report cites a source in support of a claim
then: the cited work exists with the stated author, date and publisher
its URL resolves and points at the work rather than a site root
the cited work supports what the sentence attributes to it
a citation for a work that does not exist is reported as an error

scenarios.name: The named framework was actually used
given: a report attributes its analytical framework to a practice or method
then: the selected narrative structure is reconstructable from the section sequence
the report's dimensions, criteria and recommendations derive from the practice's content
a framework named in the attribution line but unused in the report is reported as an error
a report that would read identically with no practice at all is reported as an error

scenarios.name: Diagrams are rendered SVG, not ASCII art
given: a report needs a diagram
then: it is generated by `utils/render-diagram.py` from a JSON spec kept beside the output
no fenced code block in the report contains box-drawing or ASCII box-art characters
the spec carries content and structure only, never colours, fonts, or sizes

scenarios.name: Embedded diagrams are reachable and described
given: a report embeds a diagram
then: the target path resolves relative to the report
the alt text states the diagram's claim rather than listing its boxes

scenarios.name: Structural claims carry a figure
given: a report section makes a structural claim — components and their connections, a sequence with dependencies, a containment hierarchy, or a progression through stages
then: the section carries a figure making that claim visible
a section whose content is comparative or quantitative carries a table instead of a diagram
no figure merely restates its own caption

scenarios.name: Deliverable copy uses a professional register
given: a generated report or deck
when: its headings and body copy are reviewed
then: no technical or business variable is described as choosing, deciding, picking or driving an outcome
headings state their subject or assertion without rhetorical or contrarian construction
problems are framed as prerequisites, integration and trade-offs rather than as failure or naivety
domain terminology is used in place of colloquial shorthand

scenarios.name: A section frames its parts before presenting them
given: a report section whose first content is a subsection, a table or a figure
then: two to four sentences of framing precede that first element
where the parts are a parallel set, the framing names how many there are and the role of each
the framing neither restates the heading nor merely announces that the section is beginning

scenarios.name: Figures draw the subject's instances, not the practice's types
given: the report's subject has more than one instance of a concern the practice names once (for example a production platform and a disaster recovery platform)
when: a figure covering that concern is drawn
then: each instance is a separate node named in the subject's own words
the practice concern appears as a sublabel rather than as the node label
relationships between the instances that the practice does not carry are added to the spec

scenarios.name: Embedded diagrams are captioned
given: a report embeds a diagram, which does not draw its own title
then: an italic caption follows it, numbered sequentially through the report
the caption names the figure, where the alt text states its claim

scenarios.name: Practice context loads successfully
given: the user specifies a practice, method, baseline, or .keleo bundle
then: the effective context JSON contains the baseline narrative types
the practice/method domain knowledge is accessible

scenarios.name: Missing context fails gracefully
given: the user specifies a practice that cannot be resolved
then: the skill reports the error clearly
suggests how the user can provide valid input (path to .json or .keleo file)

scenarios.name: Practices with different baselines resolve separately
given: the user specifies practices with different root baselines
then: one effective-context.json is created per distinct root baseline
the primary context drives narrative structure and report organization
supplementary contexts provide domain knowledge for specific sections

scenarios.name: Report includes in-text citations in APA 7 format
given: the effective context contains citations relevant to the report subject
when: the report makes factual claims, technical recommendations, or framework references
then: those claims are supported by APA 7 parenthetical citations (Author, Year)
citations with a URL are rendered as markdown hyperlinks `([Author, Year](URL))`
citations without a URL remain plain text `(Author, Year)`
5–15 citations appear in a standard report
citations are placed at the end of the relevant sentence, before the period

scenarios.name: Report ends with a References section
given: the report contains in-text citations
then: a "## References" section appears after the final content section
every in-text citation has a corresponding full reference entry
entries are in APA 7 format: `Author. (Year). *Title*. Source. URL`
entries are alphabetized by first author surname

scenarios.name: References are source documents, not practice metadata
given: citations are selected from the effective context
then: citations reference the original source documents (methodology papers, vendor documentation, technical guides)
no citations reference the Keleo practice, method, or baseline itself
